rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that can spread through inhalation of droplets or aerosols generated by a person with infectious pulmonary disease.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: Active TB disease and latent TB infection require different diagnostic, treatment and public-health approaches.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: Suspected or confirmed active tuberculosis is statutorily notifiable in England.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: Active-TB notifications are recorded electronically through the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System managed by UKHSA.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: Active case finding is used to identify and treat people with TB who might not otherwise seek prompt care.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: Screening for pulmonary TB can combine symptom review and chest radiography, with sputum testing where findings indicate possible disease.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: UK guidance supports latent-TB testing and treatment for eligible recent arrivals from high-incidence countries.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: UKHSA's tuberculosis reports use National Tuberculosis Surveillance System data to monitor incidence, treatment and prevention.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: TB risk depends on infectiousness, contact duration, ventilation, setting, host susceptibility, migration history, screening, treatment and timing.

rows.source: UKHSA tuberculosis notification, screening and control
rows.verified: UKHSA tuberculosis evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, screening-, treatment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level transmission probability.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: OPSS has identified baby bath seats and stands that present a serious drowning risk.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Inadequate support can allow a child to slip down or out of a bath seat.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Unsafe baby-bath products have been identified across multiple online marketplaces.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: OPSS reports classify these products within childcare articles and children's equipment.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Corrective actions have included removal of online listings.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Other corrective actions have included withdrawal from the market or recall from end users.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Product-safety reports record identifiers, listing names and product descriptions to support traceability.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Failure to meet minimum support and stability requirements can make a bath-seat product unsafe.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: Baby-bath-seat risk depends on product design, support, stability, attachment, child size, water depth, supervision, condition and use.

rows.source: OPSS baby-bath-seat drowning safety
rows.verified: OPSS baby-bath-seat evidence is product-, marketplace-, child-, use-, corrective-action- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level drowning probability.
